project: MoerEngine Async Recording / Main-Thread Submission Boundary
goal: Allow asynchronous CPU-side resource preparation and RHICommandList recording, while making Submit, Present, and Sync strictly main-thread-only. Remove cross-submit automatic state tracking and keep state tracking only inside a single submit. Cross-submit queue transfer and inter-submit resource state changes must be expressed explicitly by commands recorded by the caller.

rules_used: Do not keep fallback or compatibility implementations.
Filter validation output and only care about errors.
how_they_apply_here: Do not keep both eager GPU-side bindless initialization and deferred first-use initialization at the same time. Choose one model and delete the other path.

Do not build a generic async transport framework just to move recorded command lists from worker threads to the main thread. Use a small domain-specific result object and a promise/future style handoff.
Do not solve missing synchronization by adding WaitIdle as a safety blanket. The design must be validated by explicit submission behavior and existing tests.
Validation acceptance focuses on new validation errors and functional regressions, not warnings.
Any validation or regression scripts for this work should be run from powershell.

design_constraints.title: Submission ownership is single-threaded
design_constraints.detail: Only the main thread may call RHIExecutor::Submit(...), RHIExecutor::Sync(...), or submit Present requests.

design_constraints.title: Async work is record-only
design_constraints.detail: Worker threads may decode assets, build CPU-side metadata, create domain result objects, and record RHICommandList instances, but they may not submit GPU work.

design_constraints.title: Atomic resource creation APIs remain callable from any thread
design_constraints.detail: CreateTexture, CreateBuffer, CreateBindlessArray, and similar atomic allocation APIs may stay any-thread callable, but they must not perform hidden GPU submission as part of construction.

design_constraints.title: State tracking is intra-submit only
design_constraints.detail: Automatic resource state tracking only reasons about the command lists inside one Submit call. The runtime does not carry automatic state ownership across different Submit calls.

design_constraints.title: Cross-submit transitions are explicit
design_constraints.detail: If a resource changes queue ownership or requires a new state in a later Submit call, the caller must record the required manual transition or queue transfer commands explicitly.

design_constraints.title: Bindless initialization cannot hide a submit
design_constraints.detail: CreateBindlessArray may prepare CPU-side descriptor storage on any thread, but GPU-visible descriptor buffer initialization must be deferred into a command recorded for a later main-thread submission.

design_constraints.title: Async handoff should stay narrow
design_constraints.detail: Do not create a generic Pipe framework for all future async jobs. Use a small promise-returned loading/init payload tailored to async resource recording.

any_thread_atomic_rhi_apis: Other atomic resource allocation APIs that do not submit GPU work
allowed_async_work: Building a promise/future result that carries recorded command lists back to the main thread
main_thread_only_work: Any operation that drains, flushes, or globally synchronizes GPU work

direct_conflict.detail: RuntimeAssets starts worker-thread tasks and currently calls RHIExecutor::Submit plus WaitIdle from that async path.

latent_conflicts.detail: If async scene loading is enabled again, LoadSceneFromFileAsync can construct GPU-side scene state from worker threads.
VulkanBindlessArray construction currently performs hidden GPU submission during object creation, which violates the desired any-thread atomic API contract.

why_full_cross_submit_state_tracking_con: If the runtime tracks resource state globally across Submit calls, it must remember queue ownership and last-known state beyond the current submission boundary.
That global memory creates hidden coupling between async-produced command lists and the later main-thread submit order.
Once submission is main-thread-only and async work is record-only, it is cleaner and more predictable to make cross-submit transfer explicit in the recorded commands.

thread_model.overview: Worker threads prepare and record. The main thread owns all submission-facing actions.
rules: A worker thread may produce a ready-to-submit payload, but never consume it by calling Submit itself.
The main thread receives the payload, optionally merges it with other command lists, and performs the actual Submit/Present/Sync.

state_tracking_model.overview: Automatic state tracking is limited to one Submit call at a time.
rules: Inside a single Submit, the runtime may track state and synthesize intra-submit barriers as it already does.
Across Submit calls, the runtime does not infer the previous terminal state of a resource.
If later work depends on a prior queue transfer or state transition, the caller must record explicit commands for that boundary.
consequences: This removes hidden cross-frame and cross-job coupling from the submission runtime.
This makes async-recorded command lists portable because they do not depend on mutable global state history outside the final Submit batch.

bindless_initialization_model.overview: CreateBindlessArray becomes CPU-only construction plus deferred GPU initialization.
bindless_initialization_model.preferred_solution: Allow CreateBindlessArray on any thread, but only allocate CPU-visible state, host-side descriptor payloads, and backing resource handles. Add a dedicated InitBindlessArray command that uploads the immutable/default descriptor data when the bindless array is first used by a command list.
why_this_fits: It preserves the rule that atomic resource creation APIs are any-thread callable.
It removes the hidden submit from VulkanBindlessArray construction.
It keeps the submit boundary explicit and owned by the main thread.
required_invariants: InitBindlessArray must be one-shot per bindless array instance.
Recording or execution must guarantee InitBindlessArray happens before any command that reads bindless descriptor buffers.
The old eager-submit path in CreateBindlessArray must be deleted rather than kept as a compatibility branch.
open_implementation_choice: The one-shot insertion point can be either first UpdateBindlessArray recording or first bindless argument materialization in command recording/finalization.
Choose exactly one insertion point. Do not support multiple implicit init paths.

async_handoff_model.overview: Use a narrow promise/future handoff instead of a generic pipe.
async_handoff_model.preferred_solution: Async loading jobs return a small loading payload via promise/future. The payload should carry the recorded command list batch and the CPU-side metadata needed to publish results on the main thread.

recommended_payload_shape.name: AsyncRecordedSubmitPayload
fields: CPU-side publish data needed after submit scheduling
Optional deferred host callbacks that are local to this loading path

why_not_a_generic_pipe: The immediate problem is not generic task transport; it is a bounded handoff from async loading/init jobs back to the main thread.
A generic pipe would add framework cost and unclear ownership without solving a currently broader problem.
why_not_return_only_one_CommandList: The submit API already consumes a list of command lists.
Returning a list keeps the async payload aligned with the real submit boundary and avoids re-wrapping later when one job records more than one list.

alternatives_considered.name: Keep hidden GPU submission inside CreateBindlessArray
alternatives_considered.reason: This directly violates the new contract that atomic resource creation may happen on any thread but must not submit GPU work.

alternatives_considered.name: Force async jobs that need submission onto the main thread task queue
alternatives_considered.reason: This keeps the bad coupling where one task mixes CPU preparation and submission ownership. The new boundary should be explicit: worker records, main thread submits.

alternatives_considered.name: Introduce a generic Pipe abstraction for all async rendering jobs
alternatives_considered.reason: This is broader than the current need and violates the 'do not over-engineer' rule.

alternatives_considered.name: Keep full automatic cross-submit state tracking
alternatives_considered.reason: It preserves hidden mutable global state across submit boundaries and fights the explicit manual queue-transfer model.

execution_order: CP-01 -> first lock the ownership contract so later changes do not preserve illegal submission paths by accident.
CP-02 -> remove hidden submission from CreateBindlessArray before enabling more async callers.
CP-03 -> make deferred bindless initialization explicit and one-shot.
CP-04 -> then simplify the submission runtime to intra-submit state tracking only.
CP-05 -> define the narrow async payload model after the submit boundary is stable.
CP-06 -> migrate RuntimeAssets first because it is the direct current violation.
CP-07 -> migrate async scene/GpuScene paths next so the same bug class does not come back later.
CP-08 -> keep tests running throughout and use the final checkpoint to lock the new contract.

recommended_direction: Yes: CreateBindlessArray should become any-thread-safe only for non-submit work, and GPU-side descriptor buffer initialization should move into a deferred explicit command such as InitBindlessArray.
Yes: async jobs should hand recorded work back to the main thread with a promise/future style payload instead of performing submission inside the worker.
No: do not build a generic Pipe abstraction right now.
No: do not keep full automatic cross-submit state tracking once the design switches to explicit manual queue transfer across submit boundaries.
biggest_risks: If deferred bindless initialization has more than one implicit insertion point, the runtime will become hard to reason about and debug.
If cross-submit state tracking is only partially removed, the codebase will keep hidden dependencies on historical resource state and break the intended explicit model.
If async payloads only return a single CommandList, later multi-list jobs will need another redesign.
If RuntimeAssets is fixed but Scene/GpuScene async paths are left conceptually unchanged, the same thread-boundary violation will reappear when async scene loading is turned back on.
completion_definition: No worker-thread path calls RHIExecutor::Submit, Present, or Sync.
CreateBindlessArray performs no hidden GPU submission.
Bindless arrays initialize through an explicit one-shot recorded command before first use.
Automatic state tracking is bounded to one Submit call.
Async loading/init paths return recorded payloads to the main thread via a narrow promise/future handoff.
Existing tests still pass and validation produces no new errors.
